title: Meetings and scheduling
point: Suggest a time, check that it works, move it, decline and close, with the short phrases used to book anything from a meeting to a quick call.

sentences.ja: 木曜日のご都合はいかがですか？
sentences.note: "Does … work for you?" is the everyday way to check a time; "Is Thursday convenient?" sounds stiffer.

sentences.ja: 来週どこかで少しお話しできませんか？
sentences.text: Could we find some time to talk next week?

sentences.ja: 申し訳ないのですが、金曜日は都合がつきません。
sentences.text: I'm afraid I can't make it on Friday.
sentences.note: "I'm afraid" softens bad news, and "make it" means being able to come.

sentences.ja: 会議を3時にずらしてもいいですか？
sentences.text: Can we move the meeting to three?
sentences.note: "Move" works for any change; "push back" means later and "bring forward" means earlier.

sentences.ja: では、火曜日の10時でどうでしょう？
sentences.text: How about Tuesday at ten, then?

sentences.ja: 確認して、またご連絡します。
sentences.text: Let me check and get back to you.
sentences.note: "Get back to someone" is the standard way to promise a reply.

sentences.ja: 今日の打ち合わせ、10分ほど遅れそうです。
sentences.text: I'm going to be about ten minutes late for today's meeting.

sentences.ja: 今日の決定事項を簡単にまとめますね。
sentences.text: Let me quickly sum up what we decided today.

sentences.ja: その件はまた来週話しましょう。
sentences.text: Let's come back to that next week.

sentences.ja: では、今日はこのへんで終わりにしましょう。
sentences.text: Let's wrap it up here for today.
sentences.note: "Wrap up" is the everyday way to end a meeting or a call.
